## Proof

**CW structure of $\mathbb{CP}^n$.** The complex projective space $\mathbb{CP}^n$ admits a CW decomposition with exactly one cell $e^{2k}$ in each even dimension $2k$ for $k = 0, 1, \dots, n$, and no cells in odd dimensions. This is seen via the filtration
$$\mathbb{CP}^0 \subset \mathbb{CP}^1 \subset \cdots \subset \mathbb{CP}^n,$$
where $\mathbb{CP}^k$ is obtained from $\mathbb{CP}^{k-1}$ by attaching a single $2k$-cell (the affine chart $\mathbb{C}^k$ compactified).

**Cellular chain complex with $\mathbb{Z}_2$-coefficients.** The cellular chain group $C_{2k}(\mathbb{CP}^n; \mathbb{Z}_2) \cong \mathbb{Z}_2$ for $k = 0, \dots, n$, and $C_j = 0$ for $j$ odd or $j > 2n$. The cellular boundary map $d_j : C_j \to C_{j-1}$ has domain or codomain zero whenever $j$ is odd (since adjacent cells differ in dimension by 2, the boundary of a $2k$-cell lands in dimension $2k-1$, where $C_{2k-1} = 0$). Hence every boundary map is the zero homomorphism.

**Homology.** Since all boundary maps vanish,
$$H_k(\mathbb{CP}^n; \mathbb{Z}_2) = C_k(\mathbb{CP}^n; \mathbb{Z}_2).$$
Therefore
$$H_k(\mathbb{CP}^n; \mathbb{Z}_2) \cong \begin{cases} \mathbb{Z}_2 & k = 0, 2, 4, \dots, 2n, \\ 0 & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}$$

**Cohomology.** Since $\mathbb{Z}_2$ is a field, the universal coefficient theorem for cohomology gives $H^k(\mathbb{CP}^n; \mathbb{Z}_2) \cong \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb{Z}_2}(H_k(\mathbb{CP}^n; \mathbb{Z}_2), \mathbb{Z}_2)$ with no $\operatorname{Ext}$ term. Thus
$$H^k(\mathbb{CP}^n; \mathbb{Z}_2) \cong \begin{cases} \mathbb{Z}_2 & k = 0, 2, 4, \dots, 2n, \\ 0 & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}$$

**Cohomology ring structure.** Let $\alpha \in H^2(\mathbb{CP}^n; \mathbb{Z}_2)$ be the generator, i.e. the mod-2 reduction of the standard integral generator $c_1 \in H^2(\mathbb{CP}^n; \mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z}$ (the first Chern class of the tautological line bundle, or equivalently the generator dual to the $2$-cell).

The integral cohomology ring is $H^*(\mathbb{CP}^n; \mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z}[c_1]/(c_1^{n+1})$, with $c_1^k$ generating $H^{2k}(\mathbb{CP}^n; \mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z}$ for $0 \le k \le n$. The mod-2 reduction map $\rho: H^*(\mathbb{CP}^n; \mathbb{Z}) \to H^*(\mathbb{CP}^n; \mathbb{Z}_2)$ is a ring homomorphism (naturality of cup product with coefficient reduction). Setting $\alpha = \rho(c_1)$, we obtain
$$\alpha^k = \rho(c_1^k) = \rho(\text{generator of } H^{2k}(\mathbb{CP}^n;\mathbb{Z})).$$
Since reduction mod 2 sends the integral generator of $\mathbb{Z}$ to the generator of $\mathbb{Z}_2$, each $\alpha^k$ is the nonzero class in $H^{2k}(\mathbb{CP}^n; \mathbb{Z}_2) \cong \mathbb{Z}_2$ for $0 \le k \le n$. In particular $\alpha^k \ne 0$ for $k \le n$, and $\alpha^{n+1} = 0$ (since $H^{2n+2}(\mathbb{CP}^n; \mathbb{Z}_2) = 0$).

Because every positive-degree homogeneous element of $H^*(\mathbb{CP}^n; \mathbb{Z}_2)$ is a power of $\alpha$ (the only nonzero class in $H^{2k}$ is $\alpha^k$), the ring is generated by $\alpha$ as an $\mathbb{Z}_2$-algebra. The only relation is $\alpha^{n+1} = 0$, giving the presentation
$$\boxed{\,H^*(\mathbb{CP}^n; \mathbb{Z}_2) \cong \mathbb{Z}_2[\alpha]\,/\,(\alpha^{n+1}), \qquad |\alpha| = 2.\,}$$

This is a truncated polynomial algebra over $\mathbb{Z}_2$ on one generator of degree $2$.

### PROOF COMPLETE
